proposal.title: Recover expired Agoric IBC client 07-tendermint-129 (Stride <> Agoric, channel-148)
proposal.summary: This proposal recovers Stride's expired light client for Agoric (agoric-3), 07-tendermint-129, by substituting it with 07-tendermint-177, a freshly created and actively maintained client with compatible parameters (chain-id agoric-3, 1/3 trust level, 1540800s trusting period, 1814400s unbonding period, 600s max clock drift, matching proof specifications and upgrade path). The transfer channel pair Stride channel-148 / Agoric channel-59 (Stride connection-118 / Agoric connection-68) is the canonical Stride<>Agoric route registered in the cosmos/chain-registry. Its light clients on both chains were last updated on 2026-08-07 and have since expired (Stride 07-tendermint-129, trusting period 17.8 days; Agoric 07-tendermint-74, trusting period 11.9 days). As of 2026-09-30 the Stride-side escrow for channel-148 holds ~2,425 stATOM, ~5,920 stOSMO and ~14,268 stTIA — the backing for the stATOM/stOSMO/stTIA IBC vouchers held on Agoric — and there are 6 unresolved outbound packet commitments from Stride plus 1 from Agoric that will require relay or timeout processing after recovery. Because the same channel must be revived on both chains, a matching recovery proposal must also be submitted and passed on Agoric. Note: Stride's previous client-recovery proposals (#281/#282) received overwhelming yes support among participating voters but were rejected for failing to reach quorum; this proposal needs quorum (25% of bonded STRD) to execute. Client recovery via governance is the standard ibc-go procedure (ADR-026 / MsgRecoverClient): it copies the substitute's latest consensus state into the expired client. Recovery requires an active, newer substitute of the same client type whose trust level, unbonding period, max clock drift, proof specifications and upgrade path match the subject client; chain ID, trusting period, latest height and frozen height are permitted to differ. It moves no funds and grants no privileges to anyone; it only lets relayers resume updating the existing client so the existing channel can carry packets again.
